column3: Close to the Greek; “grasped” is rendered “comprehend,” one possible sense of the Greek verb.
Close to the Greek; NKJV supplies “was sent.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV takes “coming into the world” with “every man,” though the Greek may also go with “the Light.”
Close to the Greek; “authority” is rendered “right.”
Close to the Greek; “bloods” is rendered “blood.”
Close to the Greek; “has precedence over me” is rendered “is preferred before me.”
NKJV begins with “And,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text begins with “For.”
NKJV has “the only begotten Son,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the only begotten God.”
NKJV lacks “to him,” as does the Textus Receptus.
NKJV has “It is He who, coming after me, is preferred before me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “the One coming after me.”
NKJV reads “Bethabara,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Bethany.”
NKJV names “John,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “He sees.”
